edges.source_hint: Relayed (not independently fetched this session [UNFETCHED]) from this order and from foundry/held.json's blocking_condition on this same person ID: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Jan Baudouin de Courtenay' entry -- 'linguist who regarded language sounds as structural entities, rather than mere physical phenomena, and thus anticipated the modern linguistic concern with language structure'; 'Views expressed in his major work, Versuch einer Theorie phonetischer Alternationen (1895) ... have become a part of modern linguistic science.' edges.rationale: Both sources named by the order and the held ledger independently frame Baudouin de Courtenay's 1890s work as an early anticipation of structural/synchronic phonology -- Britannica in general-reference terms ('anticipated the modern linguistic concern with language structure', his views 'have become a part of modern linguistic science') and Honeybone in specialist-historiographic terms (naming him, jointly with Kruszewski, among 'the earliest signs (in the modern era)' of synchronic phonological work). That is the textbook shape of `influenced` -- a precursor whose work shaped the field's later development -- not a first-person founding act, and it is the target the ledger itself records as the honest, sourced alternative to the rejected morphophonology claim.
edges.uncertainty: I have not read either source live this session; both excerpts are relayed via the order and the held ledger, not independently verified. Risks QC should specifically check: (1) whether the surrounding Britannica text or the full Honeybone chapter in fact uses founder-grade language that would argue for `founded_or_formalized` instead of the more conservative `influenced` I am proposing; (2) whether the Honeybone chapter can be registered as a source, or whether an equivalent registered-family source (Wikipedia, Oxford Bibliographies -- candidates named in source_hint) independently states the same claim, since only one of the two cited sources currently has a registered provider in data/sources.json and this corpus's practice is two independent sources; (3) whether this claim, examined live, is better framed as influencing subfield:phonology specifically versus a broader structuralism/general-linguistics target -- I chose phonology because that is the target foundry/held.json itself records as supported, not because I independently re-derived it.
